title: Invoice Active Count
prompt: A C# billing worker receives a list of invoices. Write a function that returns how many items have IsActive set to true.

explanation.beginner:
Example: invoiceActiveCount([{"id":"1","isActive":true},{"id":"2","isActive":false}]) produces 1. Evaluate the selection rule for every record and preserve the qualifying values in the required order.

Compare “returns zero when none are active”: input [[{"id":"1","isActive":false}]] produces 0. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Evaluate the selection rule for every record and preserve the qualifying values in the required order.

Tempting mistake: Selecting a display position after a list changes can identify the wrong item. Use the domain key when matching two collections.

The reference uses filter. Trace the intermediate value after each operation; count repeated scans inside callbacks separately when estimating cost.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “returns zero when none are active”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
